full_judgment: 5. It is noticed by us that though the frames of both the suits one brought by the present petitioners and other one brought by opposite party No. 1-7 are declaratory in nature but their purposes and the themes are basically different and the matters in issue are not directly and substantially in issue in both the suits. It is also noticed by us that both the parties in both the suits have not based their claim under the same title. The suit land measuring 38 acres appears to have been recorded in the name of the Government in khas Khatian. It is seen from this revisional application that the opposite party Nos. 1-7 advanced their claim to the suit land on the strength of a decree passed in Partition Suit No. 127 of 1978. It is further noticed that from this revisional application that the opposite party Nos. 1-7 got preliminary decree in partition Suit No. 127 of 1978 and made the preliminary decree final and got possession through court. These are ancillary matters which we are not required to go into. On scrutiny of the plaints of both the suits, we are convinced that the matters in issue in the previously instituted suit i.e. Other Suit No. 15 of 1984, are not directly and substantially in issue in the subsequently instituted suit i.e. Other Suit No 46 of 1991. We are also convinced that the parties in both the suits advanced their claims not under the same title. We are of the view that if one criterion as envisaged in section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is found lacking the prayer for stay is to be refused and in the instant case we have already found that the matters in issue of both the suits are not directly and substantially in issue and, as such, the application for stay has been rightly and legally refused by the trial Court. The trial Court while refusing such prayer ought to have given reasons for such refusal.
